0|8099f58f1ecddf4f374f4828a3dff8397c7cbd74|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"USB: hub: Don't record a connect-change event during reset-resume
Paul Zimmerman reports that his USB Bluetooth adapter sometimes
crashes following system resume
Get-Device-Descriptor request while it is busy doing something else.
Such a request was added by commit a4f55d8b8c14 (""usb: hub: Check
device descriptor before resusciation"").  It gets sent when the hub
driver's work thread checks whether a connect-change event on an
enabled port really indicates a new device has been connected
opposed to an old device momentarily disconnecting and then
reconnecting (which can happen with xHCI host controllers
automatically enable connected ports).
The same kind of thing occurs when a port's power session is lost
during system suspend.  When the system wakes up it sees a
connect-change event on the port
persist_enabled flag was set then hub_activate() sets the device's
reset_resume flag as well as the port's bit in hub->change_bits.  The
reset-resume code then takes responsibility for checking that the same
device is still attached to the port
column2: and it does this as part of the

column1: device's resume pathway.  By the time the hub driver's work thread
starts up again
column2: the device has already been fully reinitialized and

column1: is busy doing its own thing.  There's no need for the work thread to
do the same check a second time
column2: and in fact this unnecessary check is

column1: what caused the problem that Paul observed.
Note that performing the unnecessary check is not actually a bug.
Devices are supposed to be able to send descriptors back to the host
even when they are busy doing something else.  The underlying cause of
Paul's problem lies in his Bluetooth adapter.  Nevertheless
shouldn't perform the same check twice in a row -- and as a nice side
benefit
column2: removing the extra check allows the Bluetooth adapter to work

column1: more reliably.
The work thread performs its check when it sees that the port's bit is
set in hub->change_bits.  In this situation that bit is interpreted as
though a connect-change event had occurred on the port _after_ the
reset-resume
column2: which is not what actually happened.

column1: One possible fix would be to make the reset-resume code clear the
port's bit in hub->change_bits.  But it seems simpler to just avoid
setting the bit during hub_activate() in the first place.  That's what
this patch does.
(Proving that the patch is correct when CONFIG_PM is disabled requires
a little thought.  In that setting hub_activate() will be called only
for initialization and resets
column2: since there won't be any resumes or

column1: reset-resumes.  During initialization and hub resets the hub doesn't
have any child devices
column2: and so this code path never gets executed.)
